risks: Task attributes are mutated without validation, so priority_rank() must validate the priority at call time. It should reuse validate_priority, or an equivalent check that raises ValueError. A bare dict lookup would raise KeyError instead.
validate_priority may accept values that are not strictly low, medium or high, such as non-string types or unhashable values. The rank lookup must not raise TypeError or KeyError for those.
Ordering must be stable. Sort the dict's values, which are in insertion order, by descending rank. Do not reverse an ascending sort, because that would reverse the order of ties.
The method must not mutate tasks, the dict or _next_id. It must return a new list of the same Task objects, not copies.
If a directly mutated task has an invalid priority, list_by_priority should raise ValueError. It must do so before anything changes, which is easy because nothing is mutated.
I did not read validation.py or the existing tests. Existing public behavior (AC-4) depends on adding only new methods, with no changes to existing signatures.
